art_direction.style: Scandinavian storybook illustration; watercolor + gouache on textured paper; fine ink linework; soft ambient light; muted natural colors; medium detail
art_direction.palette: Pine greens, birch whites, oak browns, soot blacks, wool greys, ice blues
art_direction.note: Each intermediate should match the style of its parent toy

set_of_blocks.name: Set Of Blocks
set_of_blocks.description: Höggva: We hew the oak log down to three identical cubes using axe, measuring by eye and hand-span.

resin_seal.name: Resin Seal
resin_seal.description: Soft seal protects corners from chipping, safe for small hands

squared_rod.name: Squared Rod
squared_rod.description: Höggva: Split and square the ash log in one action. The grain must run continuous—a sawn rod will snap under bending, but a hewn billet will yield to the sun's curve.

supple_rod.name: Supple Rod
supple_rod.description: Boil the rod in water until the lignin softens. We seethe the wood until it yields like wet leather in the hands.

ash_hoop.name: Ash Hoop
ash_hoop.description: Sveigja: Pin the hot rod into a circular frame while steam still rises. Force it into its 'memory' before it cools.

guide_stick.name: Guide Stick
guide_stick.description: Sníða: Carve the birch to a squared grip that won't slip in a frozen mitten, leaving the natural Y-fork at the tip to cradle the hoop.

wreath_base.name: Wreath Base
wreath_base.description: Flétta: Braid three green birch wands together while the sap is alive. A single bent branch is weak, but a trinity of braided birch creates a circle that will never lose its heart.

top_rough_out.name: Top Rough Out
top_rough_out.description: Höggva: Hew the dense maple log into a rough octagonal blank on the Höggvabekkr. The mass is there—the body shape with its stem socket waiting to be turned.

top_carved.name: Top Carved
top_carved.description: Renna: Shape the spinning blank on the pole lathe (Rennubekkr) at the Snikkarabekkr. Wide at equator, tapered to needle-point, with the stem socket carved at crown.

top_bleached.name: Top Bleached
top_bleached.description: Hvíta: Submerge the wood in the Ketill to bleach it white. We use the action of Sjóða (seething) to drive the milk into the grain.

swan_family_rough_outs.name: Swan Family Rough Outs
swan_family_rough_outs.description: Höggva: Hew the pine log into blocky rough-outs—one mother swan shape, three cygnet masses. The skíð still holds the bark but shows the forms waiting within.

swan_family_carved.name: Swan Family Carved
swan_family_carved.description: Sníða: On the shaving horse, pull the drawknife to release the graceful curves. The mother's arched neck, the cygnets' teardrop bodies—pine yields easily to the blade.

swan_family_bleached.name: Swan Family Bleached
swan_family_bleached.description: Hvíta: Submerge the carved swans in lye and milk. The alkaline solution bleaches pine to frost-white while milk proteins soften the grain for a matte finish.

tuned_bars.name: Tuned Bars
tuned_bars.description: Birch is a resonant tonewood; five bars carved to graduated lengths, notched underneath to tune each pitch

sound_box.name: Sound Box
sound_box.description: Pine rived into a shallow trough—the hollow amplifies and warms the tone

lye_soap.name: Lye Soap
lye_soap.description: Thin coating seals the bars without dampening vibration

pedestal_blank.name: Pedestal Blank
pedestal_blank.description: Höggva: On the Höggvabekkr, rive the oak to find the straight heart-grain and hew it into a heavy, squared block. This ensures the base will never crack from the candle's heat.

oak_pedestal.name: Oak Pedestal
oak_pedestal.description: Sníða: At the Snikkarabekkr, carve the deep socket to hold the tallow and a wide, steady foot. Etch a shallow groove at the base to cradle the vow-scroll.

wick_line.name: Wick Line
wick_line.description: Sníða: Carefully peel the inner bast fibers from the birch. Twist these into a tight cord and press them on the bench; this organic line drinks the fat better than any sinew.

etched_vow_scroll.name: Etched Vow Scroll
etched_vow_scroll.description: Grafning: Score the ancient vow into the silver skin of the Björk: 'At the darkest time, bring light.' The bark preserves the oath even as the candle burns.

cleansing_dust.name: Cleansing Dust
cleansing_dust.description: Mala: Grind the blue berries in the Mylna to a fine powder. This dust purifies the hall and fills the air with the scent of the high mountains.

scented_fat.name: Scented Fat
scented_fat.description: Sjóða: Seethe the tallow in the Ketill and fold in the juniper dust. The heat marries the mountain scent to the fat, creating a slow-burning incense.

orange_pigment.name: Orange Pigment
orange_pigment.description: Rowan berries grind to a warm orange powder—the Nisse's favorite color

orange_soap.name: Orange Soap
orange_soap.description: Cheerful orange soap, fragrant and festive. A small luxury.

small_basket.name: Small Basket
small_basket.description: Falda ok Sauma: Soften bark by hearth, fold into box, pierce corners with bone awl, stitch with wet sinew. As sinew dries, basket becomes drum-tight.

chess_billets.name: Chess Billets
chess_billets.description: Höggva: On the Höggvabekkr, hew the logs into long, squared-off bars. It is far easier to turn a square than a round log, and removing the bark protects the lathe-cord from grit.

chess_pieces_raw.name: Chess Pieces Raw
chess_pieces_raw.description: Renna: On the Rennubekkr, spin the squared billets into the 32 pieces of the armies. We turn them in 'strings' (multiple pieces on one bar) before cutting them apart.

board_planks.name: Board Planks
board_planks.description: Höggva: Hew thin, flat planks from both woods. These must be planed perfectly flat to ensure the battlefield is level.

chess_board.name: Chess Board
chess_board.description: Þrýsta: Cut the planks into 64 squares and join them edge-to-edge. Use the Press method with wedges to lock the birch and oak into their checkered marriage.

whitewash.name: Whitewash
whitewash.description: Blanda: Seethe (Sjóða) the milk and ash into a thick kalk-white. This is the 'Armor of Light' for the birch army.

wool_felt.name: Wool Felt
wool_felt.description: Hot water and agitation mat the fibers into thick, seamless felt—no edges to fray, no seams to split

wool_spool.name: Wool Spool
wool_spool.description: Strong thread for stitching features and reinforcing stress points

wool_fabric.name: Wool Fabric
wool_fabric.description: Dense plain-weave fabric—sturdy shell that won't tear or pill

set_of_blocks (oak).name: Set Of Blocks (Oak)
set_of_blocks (oak).description: Höggva: Hew oak log into identical cubes; each face ready for carving

orange_tallow_raw.name: Orange Tallow Raw
orange_tallow_raw.description: Vibrant tallow paint that soaks into carved grooves

swan_body.name: Swan Body
swan_body.description: Pine floats naturally; mother swan carved with graceful neck and hollow belly for stability

cygnet_bodies.name: Cygnet Bodies
cygnet_bodies.description: Three small cygnets—simple teardrop shapes that bob upright in water

white_pigment.name: White Pigment
white_pigment.description: Pure white base from birch ash

white_tallow_raw.name: White Tallow Raw
white_tallow_raw.description: Opaque white base coat—the snow beneath the aurora

blue_pigment.name: Blue Pigment
blue_pigment.description: Cool blue from juniper—the shimmer between the flames

blue_tallow_raw.name: Blue Tallow Raw
blue_tallow_raw.description: Aurora shimmer paint—blended into orange edges

line_flax + tow.name: Line Flax + Tow
line_flax + tow.description: Metal teeth comb retted flax; long line_flax for thread, short tow for stuffing

linen_spool.name: Linen Spool
linen_spool.description: Fine linen thread—stronger than wool, smoother to the touch

heavy_spinner_disc.name: Heavy Spinner Disc
heavy_spinner_disc.description: Dense oak disc, about 4 inches diameter—the mass stores momentum

linen_cord.name: Linen Cord
linen_cord.description: Strong twisted cord that won't snap under spinning tension

antler_y_frame.name: Antler Y Frame
antler_y_frame.description: Natural forked tine trimmed to a handle with two arms—antler's dense structure amplifies sound

bone_disc.name: Bone Disc
bone_disc.description: Flat bone discs with center holes—two pairs that clack against each other

bone_dice.name: Bone Dice
bone_dice.description: Six bone cubes carved from dense leg bone—each face marked with runes 1-6

throwing_cup.name: Throwing Cup
throwing_cup.description: Hollowed birch cylinder, palm-sized—the dice rattle satisfyingly inside

score_peg.name: Score Peg
score_peg.description: Small bone pegs for tracking wagers and scores

dice_pouch.name: Dice Pouch
dice_pouch.description: Falda ok Sauma: Fold bark into drawstring pouch, stitch with sinew to keep the set together

ash_blade.name: Ash Blade
ash_blade.description: Ash flexes on impact—safe for play-fighting. Carved with fuller groove for authenticity.

scabbard_shell.name: Scabbard Shell
scabbard_shell.description: Two birch halves hollowed to fit the blade

leather.name: Leather
leather.description: Sturdy leather for scabbard covering and belt

leather_hangers.name: Leather Hangers
leather_hangers.description: Belt loop and throat strap for the scabbard

shield_backing.name: Shield Backing
shield_backing.description: Oak planks edge-joined into a round—authentic construction

hide_glue.name: Hide Glue
hide_glue.description: Gård-Lím: the binder that makes distemper paint

purple_distemper.name: Purple Distemper
purple_distemper.description: Royal purple 'Rauðblár'—mixed blue and crimson in hide_glue binder

bone_toggle.name: Bone Toggle
bone_toggle.description: Internal anchors sewn into ear bases—allows ears to pose and hold position

bone_eyes.name: Bone Eyes
bone_eyes.description: Polished bone discs with carved pupils

tambourine_frame.name: Tambourine Frame
tambourine_frame.description: Ash ring with slots cut for jingles—flexible wood absorbs impact

board (birch).name: Board (Birch)
board (birch).description: Thin birch board for bending into hoop

supple_hoop.name: Supple Hoop
supple_hoop.description: Sjóða: Boil the birch board until pliable—must work fast before it cools

raw_hide.name: Raw Hide
raw_hide.description: Lye removes hair but keeps hide stiff—perfect for drum heads

mallet_head.name: Mallet Head
mallet_head.description: Antler head wrapped in tow for soft strike

horse_head.name: Horse Head
horse_head.description: Stylized head with open mouth—ash is light but strong

bone_teeth.name: Bone Teeth
bone_teeth.description: Sharp fangs for the open maw

board (ash).name: Board (Ash)
board (ash).description: Thin ash boards for runners—ash bends without breaking

supple_board.name: Supple Board
supple_board.description: Sjóða: Boil the ash board until pliable. ⏱ 30s timer—must bend before it cools

sleigh_runner.name: Sleigh Runner
sleigh_runner.description: Curved at front to ride over snow—the classic sleigh profile

sleigh_frame.name: Sleigh Frame
sleigh_frame.description: Heavy oak box frame for cargo—mortise-and-tenon joints

antler_finials.name: Antler Finials
antler_finials.description: Decorative finials at front—the reindeer connection

proscenium_arch.name: Proscenium Arch
proscenium_arch.description: Front frame with decorative arch—the stage window

mill_wheel.name: Mill Wheel
mill_wheel.description: Paddle wheel with carved vanes—catches stream current or hand cranking

grind_plate.name: Grind Plate
grind_plate.description: Stationary bone grinding surface—harder than wood

mill_housing.name: Mill Housing
mill_housing.description: Hollowed oak block for stability and heft

grinder_mechanism.name: Grinder Mechanism
grinder_mechanism.description: Axle transfers paddle rotation to grinding disc

hopper_cone.name: Hopper Cone
hopper_cone.description: Falda ok Sauma: Fold bark into funnel shape, stitch seam with sinew to feed material to grinder

ark_keel.name: Ark Keel
ark_keel.description: Heavy oak cradle provides ballast—the ark rights itself

crimson_casein.name: Crimson Casein
crimson_casein.description: Water-resistant crimson paint for the sail

board (oak).name: Board (Oak)
board (oak).description: Heavy oak boards for a chest that lasts generations

chest_box.name: Chest Box
chest_box.description: Sealed box construction—no gaps, no peeking

chest_body + chest_lid.name: Chest Body + Chest Lid
chest_body + chest_lid.description: Sawn horizontally after assembly—grain matches perfectly

boar_body.name: Boar Body
boar_body.description: Stocky oak body with bristled back ridge and proud snout

tusk.name: Tusk
tusk.description: Curved tusks flanking the snout—Freyr's sacred beast

axle_set.name: Axle Set
axle_set.description: Front and rear axles pinned to body

pull_strap.name: Pull Strap
pull_strap.description: Loop for towing the boar to feast

cart_body.name: Cart Body
cart_body.description: Open-top cargo box—the rolling farmstead in miniature

cord_drum.name: Cord Drum
cord_drum.description: Maple drum on drive axle wraps the suspension line

drive_axle.name: Drive Axle
drive_axle.description: Tow friction wrap on drum—wheels turn, drum turns, cord rises

sentinel_pole.name: Sentinel Pole
sentinel_pole.description: Vertical mast with pulley channel at top

nisse_figure.name: Nisse Figure
nisse_figure.description: Light birch guardian—small enough to levitate on thin cord

juften_leather.name: Juften Leather
juften_leather.description: Smoky black waterproof leather, supple and breathable

stretching_frame.name: Stretching Frame
stretching_frame.description: Taut frame holds wet leather flat during pressing

scale_press.name: Scale Press
scale_press.description: Diamond grooves carved deep—Nidhogg's scale pattern

dragon_scale_leather.name: Dragon Scale Leather
dragon_scale_leather.description: Wet leather pressed hard; grooves become permanent scales

ocean_base.name: Ocean Base
ocean_base.description: Heavy oak block carved with roller channel below, serpent slot above

lift_cam.name: Lift Cam
lift_cam.description: Eccentric disc—off-center rotation pushes serpent up and down

drive_mechanism.name: Drive Mechanism
drive_mechanism.description: Roller-axle-cam assembly: push forward, cam rotates, serpent rises

serpent_head.name: Serpent Head
serpent_head.description: Light birch Jormungandr head with open jaws—rides up through the slot

cargo_bed.name: Cargo Bed
cargo_bed.description: Five-board box with petrified joints—won't loosen

orange_tallow_sealed.name: Orange Tallow Sealed
orange_tallow_sealed.description: Waterproof ember coating—color of dying coals

rod_shaft.name: Rod Shaft
rod_shaft.description: Single-piece ash tapered tip to butt—Yggdrasil-stuff bends but never breaks

click_pawl.name: Click Pawl
click_pawl.description: Flexible antler click-check—prevents backlash, makes satisfying clicks

reel_seat.name: Reel Seat
reel_seat.description: Curved bracket clamps reel to rod shaft

fishing_reel.name: Fishing Reel
fishing_reel.description: Working centerpin reel with click drag

bone_latch.name: Bone Latch
bone_latch.description: Pivot hinge and toggle closure in one elegant piece

horse_body.name: Horse Body
horse_body.description: Hollow barrel torso—light enough to rock, strong enough to ride

curved_runner.name: Curved Runner
curved_runner.description: Seek curved grain for smooth rocking arc

rocker_base.name: Rocker Base
rocker_base.description: Two runners joined by oak crossbars—stable platform

locomotive_body.name: Locomotive Body
locomotive_body.description: Heavy oak; boiler barrel + cab. Carve 'POLAR EXPRESS' in reverse—letters stay natural oak

truck_board.name: Truck Board
truck_board.description: Small boards for wheel truck frames

wheel_truck.name: Wheel Truck
wheel_truck.description: Board frame holds 2 axles; wheels roll freely

passenger_car_body.name: Passenger Car Body
passenger_car_body.description: Carve lattice windows into sides; kids see the riders

car_roof.name: Car Roof
car_roof.description: Curved roof; lifts off for play
